newsitem.title: UK: Duchess of Kent told to rest after ME diagnosis.
newsitem.headline: Duchess of Kent told to rest after ME diagnosis.

text.p: Britain's Duchess of Kent has contracted ME, or chronic fatigue syndrome, and has withdrawn from all official engagements, her spokesman said on Thursday.
The duchess, who is married to Queen Elizabeth's cousin, the Duke of Kent, was diagnosed as suffering from the debilitating illness earlier this year but it was only publicly confirmed on Thursday.
The duchess, who converted to Catholicism in 1994, has suffered from poor health intermittently since marrying in 1961. She is 63.

The spokesman said her ME was not linked to earlier bouts of depression suffered by the duchess. These began in her 40s when she had to undergo a pregnancy termination after contracting rubella and then lost another baby. She has three children.
Chronic fatigue syndrome or ME has only recently been recognised as a genuine illness by the medical establishment.
It causes weakness or fatigue which can be disabling in very severe cases. The duchess's last public engagement was in July.
